title: Doubly robust deep kernel test on confounded digit outcomes
setting: Outcomes are 64-dim digits images with covariate-driven confounding (logistic treatment assignment on X). Treated outcomes get a fixed-norm mean shift concentrated on 1 pixel or spread over 16 pixels. A doubly robust pseudo-embedding is built from a logistic propensity and ridge outcome-embedding regressions, using random Fourier features of the kernel, with nuisances fitted on the train half. The kernel is either fixed (median bandwidth), bandwidth-tuned on the train half, or a deep kernel (MLP, 60 Adam steps) trained to maximise the cross-U power criterion. A studentised cross-U statistic on the held-out half is calibrated by sign-flips, and the metric is the rejection rate at 0.05 under the alternative (type-I rate on null replications is a diagnostic).

paper.title: Doubly Robust Deep Kernel Tests for Structured Outcomes
paper.claim: Learning deep kernel features by maximising an estimated power criterion on the doubly robust treatment-effect embedding gives higher test power than fixed and bandwidth-optimised kernels while keeping Type-I error calibrated.

metric.name: power
metric.description: Fraction of alternative-hypothesis replications (6 per run) in which the held-out sign-flip p-value is below 0.05. Diagnostics: type1 (rejection rate on null replications, should be near 0.05), mean_p_alt, mean_p_null.

factors.name: method
factors.description: Kernel on the DR pseudo-embedding: fixed Gaussian with median bandwidth, Gaussian with bandwidth chosen on the train half by the power criterion, or a deep kernel (MLP features plus characteristic component) trained on the criterion.

factors.name: shift_dims
factors.description: Number of pixels over which the fixed-norm treatment shift is spread (1 = concentrated, 16 = diffuse).

factors.name: confounding
factors.description: Strength of covariate dependence of treatment assignment; higher means poorer overlap and noisier DR weights.

factors.name: n
factors.description: Total number of units, split half into train (kernel learning and nuisances) and held-out test.
